title: The automatic pass is latched per state counter, which R245(b) rules out
summary: R245(b) rules that an automatic answer (it names the haste-step ready and the automatic pass) is latched by being unanswered, never by a state counter, because states keep arriving while an intent is outstanding. R258 says the automatic pass is latched once per actionCount via takeAutoPass, and test 70 [59] asserts that a new state number re-opens the latch. If a state with a new actionCount reaches a seat while its automatic pass is still outstanding, a second pass could go out and come back refused. The verifier confirmed it in the client: the haste ready was converted (hasteAutoOut), but the automatic pass still goes through takeAutoPass, keyed on actionCount.

title: The live action counter tells the opponent when you act inside every hidden simultaneous segment
summary: A hidden simultaneous segment is meant to show nobody the other side's plays until everyone is done (R18). R236 measured that GameState.actionCount is served live to both seats and rises on every action, so a modified client sees when its opponent acts in the resource step, the haste step and deployment. The shipped client renders nothing from it. R236 names the fix (a per-seat action counter in the engine or rooms.ts) and leaves it as the owner's call. Pinned by 205 §3d.
